general_information.Description: 1. Course Objectives: This application-based course provides undergraduate students with a strong foundation of business data analytics, focusing on data visualization, multiple regression, data mining, linear optimization models, simulation, and decision analysis, while enabling students to gain familiarity and develop mastery of these topics within the contexts of big data and artificial intelligence. 2. Course Content: Key topics include: Data Visualisation; Descriptive Analysis; Linear Regression; Predictive Data Mining and Analysis; Optimization; Big Data Analytics. 3. Activities and Teaching Methodology: Lectures, hands-on coding sessions, and individual and group projects will help students practice and develop fundamental data management and analysis techniques using Python, R, and Excel, while also exploring their application in the contexts of big data and AI to address complex, large-scale business challenges.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

description: 1. Course Objectives: This application-based course provides undergraduate students with a strong foundation of business data analytics, focusing on data visualization, multiple regression, data mining, linear optimization models, simulation, and decision analysis, while enabling students to gain familiarity and develop mastery of these topics within the contexts of big data and artificial intelligence. 2. Course Content: Key topics include: Data Visualisation; Descriptive Analysis; Linear Regression; Predictive Data Mining and Analysis; Optimization; Big Data Analytics. 3. Activities and Teaching Methodology: Lectures, hands-on coding sessions, and individual and group projects will help students practice and develop fundamental data management and analysis techniques using Python, R, and Excel, while also exploring their application in the contexts of big data and AI to address complex, large-scale business challenges.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the role of business analytics in business and financial decision-making, including analytics processes, data types, data sources, big-data/AI contexts, and basic ethical/privacy considerations.

Prepare business or financial datasets for analysis by applying foundational data-handling skills from BCP201, including importing, inspecting, cleaning, transforming, joining, and documenting data using guided tools such as Excel, Python, or R.
Apply descriptive analytics and data visualization techniques to summarize business data, identify basic patterns or outliers, and communicate insights clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Apply introductory statistical and predictive analytics methods, including basic inference, regression, forecasting, and selected classification or data-mining techniques, to support business or financial decisions.

Use introductory prescriptive analytics tools, including spreadsheet decision models, what-if analysis, simulation, and basic linear/integer optimization, to evaluate alternatives under constraints and uncertainty.

Complete a guided end-to-end business analytics project, individually and/or in teams, by framing a business problem, preparing data, selecting suitable introductory methods, interpreting results responsibly, and presenting evidence-based recommendations.

assessments.Question Type: Group project: dataset-based analysis, report/slides, presentation, and Q&A using rubric criteria
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: End-to-end business analytics project: problem framing; data preparation; descriptive/visual analysis; one suitable introductory predictive or prescriptive method; limitations; evidence-based recommendation. Groups may use Excel, Python, or R where feasible, but advanced data-mining methods and complex coding are optional/awareness-level only and should not be required.
assessments.Grading Guide: Groups complete a guided project using an approved dataset and present findings. The project should demonstrate usable business reasoning, clear communication, and explainable tool/method choices rather than technical complexity. Any Excel/Python/R outputs used must be interpreted in non-technical business language.
assessments.Note: Introduced in Session 3, checked around Session 42, finalized around Session 54, and presented in Sessions 58-59. Recommend keeping supporting materials to a project brief, rubric, and presentation guidance only.

assessments.Question Type: Individual applied analytics task with rubric criteria; concise report and/or spreadsheet/notebook output
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Data preparation, descriptive statistics, visualization, and one introductory inferential or predictive analysis selected from the covered topics. Students may use appropriate guided tools such as Excel, Python, or R, but the expected level is business interpretation, not complex coding, advanced modeling, or advanced specific programming.
assessments.Grading Guide: Students work individually on a provided or lecturer-approved dataset. They submit a concise analytics output/report explaining data preparation decisions, selected method, key results, limitations, and a business recommendation. Outputs may come from Excel, Python, R, or prepared/guided workflows, provided the student can interpret them correctly.
assessments.Note: Introduced in Session 9, supported through consultation/checkpoints, and aligned with the submission/feedback window around Sessions 30-33. The task should remain compact enough for a midterm-style take-home assessment. Do not require advanced R use as mandatory; allow it only as one feasible tool option.

assessments.Question Type: In-class guided tasks, short participation checks, and discussion/application activities
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All scheduled topics, with emphasis on guided application. Where used in the locked schedule, students may engage with prepared Excel/Python/R-style outputs or screenshots for interpretation only.
assessments.Grading Guide: Students participate in guided exercises, answer short in-class questions, discuss cases, and complete selected low-stakes tasks using the course dataset pack. The focus is engagement, interpretation, and learning process, not advanced coding performance or syntax memorization.

assessments.Question Type: MCQs; each MCQ is assigned to one CLO only
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Sessions 1-14: business analytics workflow; data types, data sources, measurement scales, ethics/privacy; dataset structure and data dictionaries; data inspection; missing values, subsetting, binning, transformations, categorical recoding; descriptive statistics; outliers; basic data visualization and chart interpretation. Questions may include simple prepared Excel/Python/R-style screenshots or outputs from the scheduled light tool-exposure sessions, but only for interpretation.
assessments.Grading Guide: Supervised in-class quiz, computer-based or paper-based. Students answer conceptual and output-interpretation MCQs; no coding from scratch, no advanced coding, and no complicated syntax memorization are required.
assessments.Note: Scheduled in Session 15. Suggested MCQ distribution for ASM breakdown: CLO1 = 5, CLO2 = 7, CLO3 = 8. R exposure is limited to reading prepared output/chart examples where relevant.

assessments.Question Type: MCQs; each MCQ is assigned to one CLO only
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Sessions 16-35, with cumulative retesting of selected foundations from Sessions 4-14: data inspection/preparation choices and descriptive/visual interpretation where needed for modeling; probability as business uncertainty; common distributions as practical tools; confidence intervals; simple hypothesis testing; regression interpretation; model fit and residual plots; forecasting; introductory classification; confusion matrix and error trade-offs; practical data-mining workflow and model-performance interpretation. Questions may include prepared Excel/Python/R-style statistical or predictive output snippets for interpretation.
assessments.Grading Guide: Supervised in-class quiz, computer-based or paper-based. Students interpret concepts, cases, charts, and prepared software-output snippets; no manual algorithm derivation, advanced coding, coding from scratch, or complicated syntax memorization is required.
assessments.Note: Scheduled in Session 36. Suggested MCQ distribution for ASM breakdown: CLO2 = 3, CLO3 = 3, CLO4 = 14. Each MCQ maps to one CLO only. Mainly predictive/statistical while retesting key data-preparation and descriptive/visual foundations needed for correct interpretation.

assessments.Question Type: MCQs; each MCQ is assigned to one CLO only
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Comprehensive coverage of core scheduled content: analytics workflow; data management and preparation; descriptive analytics and visualization; probability/inference at interpretation level; regression, forecasting, introductory classification and practical data-mining workflow; spreadsheet modeling, simulation, and optimization at application/interpretation level. Questions may include prepared Excel/Python/R-style output snippets, charts, or model summaries for interpretation.
assessments.Grading Guide: Individual final exam with MCQs. Questions emphasize concept recognition, case interpretation, software-output reading, chart/model interpretation, and decision implications. No coding from scratch, no complicated syntax memorization, and no advanced algorithm derivation are required.
assessments.Note: Final practice appears in Sessions 56-57. Suggested MCQ distribution for ASM breakdown: CLO1 = 5, CLO2 = 7, CLO3 = 8, CLO4 = 18, CLO5 = 12. Excel/Python/R-style output is included only as prepared output-reading practice.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: Translate a practical business question into a basic analytics workflow by identifying the decision to be supported, the data needed, the preparation and visualization steps, and the type of insight managers can use.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: Frame a business analytics problem by identifying the decision context, stakeholders, available data, analytics objective, and basic ethical or privacy risks.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: Identify data types, measurement scales, data sources, and file formats in business or financial datasets, and explain how these choices affect later analysis.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4
constructive_questions.Details: Import, inspect, clean, transform, and document a simple business dataset using guided Excel, Python, or R workflows.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5
constructive_questions.Details: Use descriptive statistics to summarize business performance, variability, outliers, and relationships among variables.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6
constructive_questions.Details: Choose and create appropriate visualizations for business data, and explain how chart design can clarify or mislead business interpretation.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7
constructive_questions.Details: Use basic probability and uncertainty concepts to describe business or financial risks in practical decision situations.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8
constructive_questions.Details: Interpret confidence intervals and simple hypothesis tests as evidence for business comparisons, without relying on advanced mathematical derivations.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9
constructive_questions.Details: Build and interpret a simple linear regression model for a business or financial prediction problem using guided software output.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10
constructive_questions.Details: Interpret a multiple regression model with business variables, including coefficient meaning, model fit, and limitations of prediction.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11
constructive_questions.Details: Diagnose and improve a regression analysis by checking basic assumptions, unusual observations, and practical usefulness for decision-making.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12
constructive_questions.Details: Create and interpret a basic time-series forecast using trend, seasonality, and simple model-selection logic.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the data-mining workflow by preparing training and validation data and choosing suitable performance measures for a business prediction task.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14
constructive_questions.Details: Apply an introductory classification method, such as logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, or naïve Bayes, and interpret prediction results in business terms.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15
constructive_questions.Details: Use introductory decision trees, clustering, or association rules to discover useful customer, product, or market patterns.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16
constructive_questions.Details: Construct a spreadsheet decision model and use what-if, goal-seek, or scenario analysis to compare business alternatives.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17
constructive_questions.Details: Use Monte Carlo simulation to model uncertainty and communicate likely outcome ranges for a business or financial decision.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18
constructive_questions.Details: Formulate and solve a basic linear programming problem by defining decision variables, an objective function, and practical constraints.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19
constructive_questions.Details: Interpret basic optimization applications, such as budgeting, transportation, assignment, workforce scheduling, or facility-location decisions.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20
constructive_questions.Details: Complete and defend a guided business analytics project by connecting problem framing, data preparation, method selection, findings, limitations, and recommendations.
